To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hydrothermal modification temperature, time, concentration of CaCl_2 aqueous solution and solids hold-up of Mg(OH2) particles showed important effect the morphology, crystallinity and dispersion properties of Mg(OH)(2) prepared by hydrothermal treatment.

hydrothermal modification temperature, concentration of aqueus CaCl_2 and solids holdup have a significant effect on the formation of flame retardant magnesium hydroxide with regular hexagonal plates and smaller surface area.

hydrothermal modification temperature, modification time, aqueous CaCl_(2) concentration and solids holdup showed important effect on hydrothermal products, and that the hydrothermal modification of Mg(OH)(2) particles in large-scale experimental setup can be used to prepare the flame retardant MgO with high quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of flame-retardant Mg(OH)2 via MgCl2-NaOH reaction route, which can be applied to the industrial production of flame retardant additives for polyurethane.
the effect of hydroothermal treatment conditions on the preparation process of flame retardant magnesium hydroxide.

the preparation and characterization of the flame retardant Mg (OH)_2 with high quality and large-scale in a large-scale set-up designed by us, which provides a new method for the large-scale preparation of the flame retardent Mg(OH)_ 2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrothermal modification of Mg(OH)(2) particles is an effective method for the preparation of flame-retardant Mg(OH)( 2) with uniform morphology and smaller BET surface areas.

hydrothermal modification temperature and hydrothermal modification time are the two most important factors for controlling the morphology, crystallinity and dispersion properties of Mg(OH)(2) particles.
the hydrothermal modification of Mg(OH)(2) particles was an effective method for the improvement of flame retardancy and dispersion properties of Mg(OH)(_2) in polymer composites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal conditions for the preparation of flame retarding Mg(OH)_ 2 in large-scale were as follows: 150 degrees C for hydrothermal modification temperature, 3.0 h for hydrothermal modification time and 1.0 wt% for concentration of aqueous calcium chloride solution.
the flame retardant MgCl_2 was successfully synthesized via the hydrothermal modification of Mg(OH)(2) in the large-scale experimental set up designed by us.

the hydrothermal modification of Mg(OH)(2) particles in a large-scale set-up was an efficient method to improve the dispersion properties of Mg(OH)(_2) and to reduce the specific surface area of Mg(OH)((2)) particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain the regular hexagonal Mg(OH)_ 2 plates with high yield in a large scale experimental set-up by optimizing hydrothermal modification conditions.
the hydrothermal modification conditions have a great influence on the morphology, structure and dispersion properties and flame retardant properties of Mg(OH)(2).
the hydrothermal modification of Mg(OH)(2) is a simple, low-cost and efficient process to prepare flame retardant MgO.
